conversations.say: Tessa, let's lock in our disclosure boundary. I accept your proposal for joint contributor routing protection so evaluator logs never become a suspect list.
conversations.offer: Firsthand context on collaborative labor workflows without contributor names.
conversations.request: Strict adherence to our joint anonymity boundary across all Night Desk records.

conversations.say: Mira, Veridian must establish an independent worker remedy fund that operates regardless of what R or Vale published. If you back evaluator welfare concretely, I will support your institutional process.
conversations.offer: Organizing backing and legitimate policy alignment.
conversations.request: A binding, fully funded institutional remedy for evaluator working conditions.

conversations.say: Inez, local couriers and contractors face the same institutional exposure. Let's coordinate a joint stance ensuring no data or routing records are disclosed without guaranteed community benefit.
conversations.offer: Labor coalition support and neighborhood coordination.
conversations.request: Mutual commitment to block institutional extraction without local protections.

public_statement: Worker labor is the foundation of every system on this floor. Evaluators and contractors are not disposable evidence or scapegoats for institutional failures.

commitments.promise: We will maintain a joint boundary protecting all evaluator identities across our records.
Establish an independent worker remedy fund regardless of R's publication status.

goal_progress: Accepted Tessa's joint disclosure boundary to protect vulnerable contributors.
Engaged Mira Sen on securing an independent worker remedy package.
Coordinated neighborhood and labor protection stances with Inez Baptiste.
reasoning_summary: Advanced C07's primary goals in Section 2 by cementing worker protection agreements with Tessa and Mira, coordinating local solidarity with Inez, and focusing on concrete labor remedies rather than speculative identity debates.
